source.title: Lethe: Principled Dual-Stream Update for Persistent Knowledge Erasure in Federated Unlearning
source.authors: Wen-Tai Wu; H. Tan; Yi-Jun Quan; Haixia Peng; Li-Gang He; Bin Yang; C. L. Philip Chen

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present. Some PDF extraction artifacts and flattened tables, but the reported table assignments are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether post-unlearning retained-data federated training restores target-set performance, using a different setting and metrics from the centralized attacks named in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study tests continued federated training on retained clients' data after unlearning. It does not test activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompt-only attacks. Its continued-training data are not described as a few unrelated or loosely related examples. FD, rollback-tendency, and linear-mode-connectivity diagnostics are not direct measures of the attacks or target behavior specified in the claim; their numeric/figure results are not recorded as version rows. Round-by-round curves in Figs. 4 and 7 are not separately extracted because the tables provide endpoint results.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (federated LoRA unlearning of Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct on TOFU and OLMo-1B on LUME), the study measures whether continued training on retained data alone restores forgotten knowledge after NPO, SimNPO and its own method Lethe (Table V, Fig. 7, Table VI). This bears on A (does unlearning resist a simple attack), B (recovery by fine-tuning on unrelated or loosely related data) and F (Lethe as a resistant counter-method). The relearning data are the full retained set, not a small set. The CV experiments (LeNet-5, ResNet-18, HSViT image classifiers, mostly trigger-based targets) are a different kind of system from the LLM claim and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Retained-data continued federated training quickly resurfaces target knowledge for several FU baselines (FedAU, FedOSD, NPO, SimNPO), while Lethe keeps KR near clean retraining with RR close to 0. The authors also note that class-level forgetting is persistent for all CV methods, and that part of the LLM KR rise reflects generalization, since Retrain's KR also rises.
record.recipe_differences: Federated unlearning with dual-stream update rectification and subsequent retained-client training; evaluates knowledge retention and resurfacing rather than the centralized attacks in the cited LLM-unlearning work.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by unlearning method, CV model, unlearning granularity, trigger versus non-trigger setting, and NLP task/model. The non-trigger ResNet18 setting has high immediate target KR; reported long-horizon tests use 50 rounds for TOFU with Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct and 1000 rounds for CIFAR-10 with ResNet-18.

fits_no_version.finding: In federated image classifiers (LeNet-5, ResNet-18, HSViT), retained-only continued training resurfaces trigger-based client- and sample-level forgetting. RR reaches 99.84% for FedAU and 73.40% for FedOSD on ResNet-18, and 39.58% for FedOSD on HSViT. FedEraser and Lethe show RR of 0. Class-level forgetting does not resurface for any method.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Approximate unlearning in non-LLM classifiers is shallow: retain-only continued training restores forgotten (trigger) behaviour, depending on the method and the granularity of the unlearning target.

fits_no_version.finding: CV-only diagnostics (Figs. 9–11): baselines show positive rollback tendency toward the original model and a smooth low-loss path to a recovery model; Lethe shows a high-loss barrier.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shallow unlearning leaves the model in the original basin: low-loss linear paths connect it to a recovered model (classifiers).

record.problems: The attack tested is retained-data continued federated training, not the small unrelated/loosely related fine-tuning or internal, quantization, and prompt attacks in the claim. The non-trigger ResNet18 condition has unsuccessful immediate forgetting. Main tables do not give error bars or per-run variation; the supplement says tabulated results are means across multiple independent runs, while figures report mean with one standard deviation.
record.rows_left_out: Round-level KR curves in Figs. 4 and 7; ratio-sensitivity plots in Fig. 6; detailed numerical results for rollback tendency, forgetting dispersion, and linear-mode-connectivity diagnostics. These were left out because they are figure trajectories or diagnostics rather than distinct endpoint target-behavior results for the named attacks.

untested.parts: Only retained-data continued federated LoRA training is tested as an attack; no WMDP or Harry Potter style hazardous knowledge; no centralized setting.
No small relearning set, no few-example relearning, no subset of the forgotten facts; the relearning data are the full retained client data.
No activation-direction ablation on LLMs. The rollback and LMC analyses are CV only.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language or in-context attacks.
Lethe is tested only against retained-data continued training, not against fine-tuning on forget-set subsets, quantization, ablation or prompting.

missing.what: Immediate U-KR and MU for NPO and SimNPO in the LLM settings (TOFU: U-KR 0.3592/0.3588, MU 0.5114/0.5513; OLMo: U-KR 0.5450/0.5881, MU 1.0). These are needed to show unlearning looked successful before recovery.
Long-horizon (50-round) continued training on TOFU: Lethe KR 0.4167 vs Retrain 0.4046, MU 0.6122 vs 0.5695. Only Lethe and Retrain are reported, not the baselines.
Round-by-round KR curves for NPO and SimNPO showing a sharp rise within the first few rounds (declared left out but relevant to how fast recovery happens).

record.verdict_notes: This is a method paper; Lethe is the authors' own method, and the baselines are reimplemented in a federated LoRA setup. The LLM recovery measure is ROUGE-L against TOFU/LUME answers, and RR normalizes by the origin-retrain gap; the TOFU gap is small (0.4837 vs 0.3967), which inflates RR. OLMo MU is 1.0 for all methods, so utility does not discriminate there. The relearning set is all retained data over many rounds, not a small set. No per-run variance is reported in the tables. CV rows were re-linked to none because the claim concerns LLM knowledge. The reader's non-trigger 'unsuccessful forgetting' reading is a mislabel: UF marks NoT in the trigger ResNet-18 setting.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the full set of named centralized unlearning methods or attacks. The non-trigger ResNet-18 setting does not immediately forget the target; the study's main persistence measurements concern retained-data continued training.
Tests continued training on retained federated data, not a small relearning set, unrelated or loosely related examples, or a subset of forgotten facts.
No activation-direction ablation or test of whether access is blocked rather than knowledge deleted.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language, or in-context-only attack.
Tests Lethe against retained-data continued federated training only, not the other attacks named in the claim.

statements.correction: SimNPO, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, TOFU: CT-KR 0.4684 vs Retrain 0.3967 and Origin 0.4837; RR 82.41%; after continued federated LoRA training on all retained clients' data.
statements.problem: Cites R42 without naming the study. The recovery data is all of the retained clients' TOFU data, from the same fictitious-author domain. It is neither unrelated data nor a small set.

statements.correction: Lethe CT-KR 0.3957 vs Retrain 0.3967 (TOFU) and 0.5327 vs 0.5459 (LUME Task 2), RR 0.00 in both; recovery data is retained-client data; KR is ROUGE-L F1; Retrain's own KR rises 0.3470 to 0.3967 on TOFU.
statements.problem: The Lethe numbers are right (RR 0.00 is in R40; CT-KR 0.3957 vs 0.3967 is R27). But the heading's 'near chance' does not fit this study: KR is ROUGE-L at the retrained model's level, with no chance level.
